transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

My mind just doesn’t seem to work the way it used to—I can’t think straight or make simple decisions anymore. It just feels like my head is always foggy, and even the smallest tasks feel completely overwhelming.

Can you tell me more about when you first noticed these changes in your thinking and decision-making, and have you experienced any significant stressful events or emotional difficulties around that time?

These changes started about a year and a half ago, right when my older sister developed some serious heart problems. I had to take on coordinating all her medical appointments and medications, which became incredibly stressful and overwhelming. The strain of her illness and trying to manage everything really seemed to trigger this mental fogginess.

Did you experience any persistent and distressing emotions, such as sadness, hopelessness, or guilt, in addition to the mental fogginess and difficulty with decision-making, after your sister's illness and your subsequent caregiving responsibilities began?

Yes, I've had this deep, persistent sadness for over a year now. I wake up most days with a heavy, sinking feeling in my chest, feeling like there's no point to the day and that I'm just useless. It stays with me from the moment I wake up until I go to sleep.
Have you also noticed a decrease in interest or pleasure in activities that you once enjoyed, or has your ability to experience pleasure remained relatively intact despite your other symptoms?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in the things I used to love, like my watercolor classes, quilting circles, and genealogy trips. Even when I have the free time, I just can't bring myself to go anymore. Being around people and trying to enjoy myself feels like way too much effort and just isn't worth it.

Can you tell me if these feelings of sadness, loss of interest, and mental fogginess have been continuous over the past year and a half, or have there been periods where you felt somewhat better in between?

The heavy sadness and loss of interest have been there almost constantly for over a year, even during times when my thinking wasn't quite as jumbled. But early on, there was a brief stretch of a few weeks where I wasn't feeling sad yet and still enjoyed my quilting, though I was already sure the hospital staff were working against us.

Can you clarify if there have been any distinct periods of at least two months where you didn't experience any of these depressive symptoms, such as the sadness, loss of interest, or mental fogginess, over the past year and a half?

No, I haven't had any long breaks or two-month periods where I felt free of these symptoms. Since they started a little over a year ago, the heavy sadness and lack of interest have been present almost constantly, without any real relief. It has just been a continuous weight most days.

Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood or functioning that lasted for at least two months since your symptoms began, or have the symptoms been persistent without any notable remission?

No, I haven't had any periods of improvement like that at all. The heavy mood, lack of interest, and mental fogginess have been persistent and present almost all the time since they started about a year and a half ago. There has been no real break from it.

Have you experienced any episodes of significant mood elevation or irritability, where you felt unusually happy, energetic, or agitated, in contrast to your usual depressive symptoms, over the past year and a half?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. My mood has been consistently low, heavy, and slow, and I've never had any periods of high energy or unusual happiness over the past year and a half. It has just been a constant feeling of being weighed down.

You've mentioned that your symptoms have been persistent for over a year and a half without any significant periods of improvement, but can you tell me if you've had any episodes of depression in the past, before your sister's illness, or if this is the first time you've experienced such a prolonged period of depressive symptoms?
No, this is the very first time I have ever experienced anything like this. I never had these kinds of dark, heavy feelings or depression before my sister got sick.
